messages:
alex wong: evening -> midnight oncall handoff. Quick summary: we had a customer-facing spike in 502s from the hosted API between ~18:12-18:45 UTC due to a routing table flapping event on region-eu-primary; impacted ~12% of requests (mainly gen endpoints). Primary mitigation applied: automated fallback to region-us for compatible sessions + temporary throttling of large-batch requests. Current status: traffic normalized ~18:50, error rate steady at baseline, but some stale KV cache shards still show elevated miss rate. Follow-ups and owners below. TL;DR: customer impact was limited, no data loss, some increased latency for affected sessions. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: ALERT 18:14 UTC - 502 surge detected - service: redwood-hosted-api - symptom: ~12% 502s, error-class: routing/egress - page: @oncall. Incident ID: INC-2026-1143.

maria gonzalez: saw the alert, jumped on the bridge at 18:16. Root cause appears to be partial BGP flap on the region-eu-primary egress node that rebalanced LB pools and caused a handful of long-lived worker connections to reset. The routing team pushed a soft route withdraw at 18:22 which reduced churn.

ops-bot: mitigation actions executed: 
- failover policy applied: route_compat_fallback=enabled at 18:23
- throttle rule added: max_batch_tokens=8000 for user-tier=free at 18:24
- cache_prefetch disabled for region-eu at 18:25
(see runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-flap)

jamal singh: noted elevated KV miss rate in eu-cache-2 (shard 7) starting 18:20. I flushed the hot keys and warmed prefetched prefixes for the top 100 routes. Miss rate dropped ~70% by 18:40. Still seeing occasional slow gets (p99 ~210ms vs baseline 45ms).

sofia li: customer-impact assessment - looking up top affected customers now. Early look: three mid-market customers had timeouts on long polls (30s+) between 18:15-18:35; one support ticket opened, CS notified. No broad customer data errors.

alex wong: immediate follow-ups (owners):
- routing postmortem + BGP delta: owner @maria gonzalez
- KV cache shard health + rebalancing: owner @jamal singh
- customer comms summary + tickets: owner @sofia li
- verify fallback coverage & canary policy: owner @alex wong

maria gonzalez: initial notes for postmortem: need to correlate BGP route updates with our LB healthchecks and worker reconnects. Also check why route_compat_fallback didn't trigger earlier for some sessions (policy mismatch on legacy-client). Action: run grep over control-plane logs and dump route-change timeline.

jamal singh: command I ran to flush hot keys (internal):
```
curl -X POST "https://cache-admin.redwood.internal/shard/7/flush" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"prefixes": ["/kv/prefix/top_routes_"]}'
```
Also put a soft restart on cache worker 7a at 18:35 which cleared a connection leak. Note: schedule a replacement of that worker; it's churny.

sofia li: communicated to CS at 18:55 with the following blurb for affected customers: "We experienced a transient routing disruption in EU that caused elevated errors and some timeouts between 18:12-18:50 UTC. Failovers and throttles were applied automatically; we did not observe data loss. Our engineering team is following up and will share a postmortem."

alex wong: coverage note — tomorrow morning we'll have a coverage gap between 07:00-10:00 UTC: maria is on PTO, and our rotation shows only one primary in-region for EU. I propose swap: @jamal singh take EU morning primary and @alex wong be secondary for that window. Please confirm.

maria gonzalez: confirmed PTO. I can handover any remaining artifacts before EOD local.

jamal singh: I can take EU morning primary, will be reachable on pager and phone. I'll validate cache shard rebalancing at 07:15 and run a synthetic load to ensure cold starts are healthy.

alex wong: runbook pointers for whoever inherits this:
- Routing flap runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-flap (steps 1-6 to verify failover executed and route withdraws)
- KV cache triage: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache#hot-shard (includes the `flush` endpoint and worker-restart checklist)
- Customer comms template: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/customer-incident-template

maria gonzalez: checklist items I've left in the incident doc:
- route-change timeline (control-plane logs) ✅
- affected session ids sample (csv) ✅
- list of customers impacted (CS handoff) ✅
- tentative RCA hypothesis (BGP flap -> LB churn -> stale connections) in progress

sofia li: open action items (short):
- SOFT-1: CS follow-up email draft for affected customers (owner: sofia) - due EOD
- TECH-1: replace cache worker 7a and monitor shard stability (owner: jamal) - schedule maintenance
- TECH-2: verify legacy-client fallback policy mapping (owner: alex) - verify by 09:30 UTC tomorrow
- POSTMORTEM: full incident write-up (owner: maria) - due in 72h

alex wong: next steps for incoming shift: please pick up the incident doc in the incidents folder (INC-2026-1143) in Confluence, check TECH-1/TECH-2 status at 07:15 UTC, and escalate to routing if the p95 of connect-resets > 3% for more than 10 minutes. If anything looks off, call paging channel and open a new bridge.

jamal singh: copying my quick diagnostic commands into the thread for morning checks:
```
# check cache shard latency
curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/query?metric=kv_shard_p99&shard=7 | jq .value
# check connect reset rate
kubectl logs -n edge svc-lb --since=2h | grep 'connect reset' | wc -l
```

alex wong: thanks all. I'll handoff formally at 00:00 UTC. If you take the morning EU slot, ping me once you validate TECH-2. :pray:
